suggestions.title: Monday is blank except the scale — fill in 8/17. Rough numbers count.

rationale.science: Adherence is the meta-lever: when a rate stalls, check the log before blaming metabolism — and you cannot check a log with a hole in it (Alhassan 2008).
rationale.data: 2026-08-17 has your 164.2 weigh-in and nothing else — no calories, no protein, no steps, no sleep night, and no session on a lower day. Every other day from 8/9 to 8/16 is complete.
rationale.relationship: The forecast I filed for Friday rests on four clean weekday logs and Monday is one of the four. A missing day does not push the answer one way or the other — it makes the test unanswerable in both directions. You filled 8/13 in the day after I asked and that is the entry that made last week readable at all.

suggestions.predict: Put Monday in — food, protein, steps, and whether you trained — and Friday's test gives a real verdict either way. Leave it blank and the honest answer on Friday is 'untestable', not a number, and a fourth week goes by without a clean read on your own weekday pace.

suggestions.title: Pick the hip thrust's load in SETUP before Friday — it debuts on the one session five other lifts restart from.

rationale.science: On a cut you defend load rather than chase volume, and a lift you cannot compare across sessions cannot tell you whether you are defending it (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024).
rationale.data: exercises.hipthrust.w is still null. It sat in the 8/14 skipped list, its start date (8/17) passed with no session logged, and its arrival is what started fresh four-session baselines on calves, hanging, abs, ham and extension.
rationale.relationship: Your record already has both outcomes of this exact decision. Hack squat was entered at 190 on the gym floor, the app said the stack topped out there, and the record had to be corrected to the 200 you actually lifted. Ham curl was checked in SETUP first and debuted clean at 125 x 11,9,9.

suggestions.predict: Check the machine's rungs and set the load before Friday and the hip thrust's first outing banks a clean line the seam can measure everything else from. Guess it on the floor and you get either a WORKING LOAD RECONCILED amendment like the hack, or a debut that lands wrong on the single session where five other lifts are also starting over — which is the one place a wrong number cannot be untangled afterwards.
